messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order."

So we have "raw" input; we need to interpret accordingly.

Given knowledge_cutoff = 100. All reports have received_time <= knowledge_cutoff (they are all <= 100). So all are visible.

Each event_id appears only once (revision 1). No later revisions. So highest revision per event_id is the same revision.

Then we filter those events to only those with event_time <= target_time (target_time = 100). All events times are: 11,22,26,36,46,47,48,52,58,73,82,84. All <= 100. So we include all.

Now we need to apply these events in order sorted by (event_time, event_id). Since event_time values are all distinct (no ties). So order is by event_time ascending.

We have initial_stock = 20.

We need to simulate receipts (+quantity); demands consume min(stock, quantity), any unmet quantity is lost (lost sales). Stockout is defined as strictly positive unmet demand (i.e., a demand that cannot be fully met). Not mere ending with zero stock after meeting demand.

We also need to compute historical_lost: total unmet demand up through target_time using visible revisions (the ones we used). Also need stock_at_target (stock after processing those events). That is the stock after all events up to target_time (which includes all events because target_time = 100 > all). So stock_at_target = stock after processing all historical events.

Then "After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario." So we start with stock_at_target as the starting stock for the future scenario and apply those future events (receipts, demands) sorted by event_time and event_id. The future_schedule events all have unique event_id but may have same event_time? Let's check: times: 101 (receipt), 105 (demand), 107 (receipt), 114 (receipt), 115 (demand), 117 (demand), 121 (receipt), 122 (demand), 124 (receipt), 126 (demand), 127 (receipt), 129 (demand). All distinct.

We need to compute stock after all future events up to horizon_time 130? horizon_time = 130. The future events go up to 129, which is <= horizon_time. So we apply all of them. Compute stock_at_horizon = final stock after processing all future events (i.e., at horizon_time). Actually horizon_time defines the end of scenario horizon. The future schedule covers up to time 130. So stock_at_horizon is final stock after applying all future_schedule events with event_time <= horizon_time. Since all events in schedule have event_time <= 129 <= 130, we include all. So stock_at_horizon = final stock after all future events.

We need to compute future_lost: total unmet demand for the future scenario only (i.e., lost sales due to future demands). Do we also count any unmet demand from historical events? No; we separate. So future_lost is sum of unmet demand from future_schedule events only.

First_future_stockout_time: earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand (i.e., a demand that couldn't be fully satisfied). If no future demand has unmet portion, answer -1.

We also need to compute total historical_lost across all historical events up to target_time.
